## feat/issue-158-agent-prompt-loader-pipeline-handoffs

**Synthesis Date:** 2026-04-24  
**Branch:** `feat/issue-158-agent-prompt-loader-pipeline-handoffs`  
**Base:** `development`  
**Models:** Claude Sonnet 4.6 · GPT 5.4 · Gemini 3.1 Pro  
**Raw reports:** `2026-04-24-pr167-claude-raw.md` · `2026-04-24-pr167-gpt-raw.md` · `2026-04-24-pr167-gemini-raw.md`

---

## Synthesis Overview

PR #167 introduces the first Python-native migration slice: relocating agent system prompts from `.opencode/agents/` to `prompts/agents/`, adding a typed pipeline handoff layer (`src/application/pipeline/handoffs.py`), and a caching agent prompt loader (`src/infrastructure/prompts/agent_prompt_loader.py`). All three models agreed that the core implementation is clean, well-typed, and well-covered by tests, and all three independently flagged the same root problem: the agent prompt relocation was not followed through to live documentation surfaces — README.md and AGENTS.md still instruct readers to look in the now-empty `.opencode/agents/` directory. Beyond this unanimous finding, GPT surfaced two additional stale references (architecture notes and a savepoint comment) that the other reviewers missed, bringing the total corrective surface wider than Claude or Gemini identified.

**Model Agreement Score:** 7/10 — strong consensus on the central relocation documentation gap, divergence on severity framing and on the scope of secondary stale references.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

```
[U-W-01] Stale .opencode/agents/ references in live developer documentation
Severity: Warning (consensus — see Divergence [D-01] for severity split)
Category: Documentation
Files: README.md · AGENTS.md
Lines: README.md:189; AGENTS.md:28
Detail: This PR empties .opencode/agents/ (only .gitkeep remains) and relocates all
agent system prompts to prompts/agents/. Two high-visibility documentation files were
not updated to reflect that change:

  • README.md line 189 still reads: "Agents (.opencode/agents/): story-orchestrator,
    outline-planner, chapter-writer"
  • AGENTS.md line 28 still reads: "Story generation agents are defined in
    .opencode/agents/."

AGENTS.md is particularly high-risk because it is injected into every Copilot context
via .github/copilot-instructions.md. Any agent or developer consulting these files will
navigate to a now-empty directory. Both were confirmed stale via grep verification.
Models: Claude ✓ GPT ✓ Gemini ✓
Suggestion: Update README.md line 189 to reference prompts/agents/. Update AGENTS.md
line 28 to reference prompts/agents/ and note that prompt bodies are loaded via
src/infrastructure/prompts/agent_prompt_loader.py.
```

---

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-W-01] Relocation regression test does not adequately protect the moved prompt set
Severity: Warning
Category: Testing
File: tests/unit/test_prompt_relocation.py
Lines: 41-58 (test_prompt_subdirectories_exist); 107-111 (test_prompt_file_count)
Detail: Two independent test weaknesses were surfaced:

  1. test_prompt_subdirectories_exist (lines 41-58): the expected_subdirs list covers
     "chapters", "characters", "multistep", "outline", etc. but does not include
     "agents". Deletion of the entire prompts/agents/ directory would not be caught
     by this structural test.

  2. test_prompt_file_count (lines 107-111): the assertion was loosened to
     `len(md_files) >= 148`. As the test docstring and migration PRD both state, the
     goal is to verify the relocated prompt set is preserved — a floor count cannot
     prove that; any unrelated Markdown file added anywhere under prompts/ masks a
     missing agent prompt file.

Both weaknesses were independently verified in the actual test file.
Models: GPT ✓ Claude ✓ Gemini ✗
Dissenting view: Gemini did not mention the test coverage gap. Claude raised the
missing "agents" subdir as a Suggestion; GPT escalated the weakened count assertion
to Warning. The synthesis treats the combined gap as Warning-level because a regression
test that cannot catch the specific regression it was written for is a substantive
testing defect, not merely a style issue.
Suggestion: (a) Add "agents" to the expected_subdirs list in
test_prompt_subdirectories_exist. (b) Replace or augment the count assertion in
test_prompt_file_count with an explicit check that each expected agent prompt file
exists under prompts/agents/ (e.g., assert each stem from the original .opencode/agents/
manifest is present).
```

```
[S-I-03] .github/notes/architecture.md also contains stale .opencode/agents/ references
Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation
File: .github/notes/architecture.md
Lines: 112-118
Detail: Lines 112-118 describe "Three agents defined in .opencode/agents/" and table

Assessment: Confirmed genuine. Claude and Gemini scoped their stale-reference findings
to README.md and AGENTS.md; GPT's broader scan also flagged architecture.md and the
```

```
[S-I-04] src/infrastructure/prompts/ lacks __init__.py — inconsistent with siblings
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style
File: src/infrastructure/prompts/agent_prompt_loader.py
Lines: general
Detail: Every peer sub-package under src/infrastructure/ (logging/, providers/,
savepoints/, storage/) has an __init__.py. The prompts/ directory still has none,
causing an inconsistency that may confuse tooling and new contributors. File search
confirmed __init__.py is absent. Imports work via Python 3.3+ namespace packages but
the pattern is inconsistent.
Model: Claude
Assessment: Confirmed genuine minor inconsistency. This is a pre-existing gap worsened
by this PR adding a new module without also adding the package marker.
Suggestion: Add an empty src/infrastructure/prompts/__init__.py.
```

```
[S-I-05] No path traversal guard on the name parameter in load_agent_prompt()
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Security
File: src/infrastructure/prompts/agent_prompt_loader.py
Lines: 19-20
Detail: name is used directly in file_path = AGENTS_DIR / f"{name}.md". A value
containing path separators (e.g., "../config/secrets") could escape AGENTS_DIR.
Current call sites use hardcoded string literals, so the practical risk today is
negligible. The concern is forward-looking: if the loader is extended to accept
user-supplied names (CLI flag, API input) the boundary becomes a path traversal vector.
Model: Claude
Assessment: Plausible low-priority finding. Not a current vulnerability given hardcoded
call sites, but cheap to guard and documents the contract explicitly.
Suggestion: Add before path construction:
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name or name.startswith("."):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid agent name: {name!r}")
```

## Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Severity of the stale documentation finding
Claude says: Two separate Warnings (W-01 for README.md, W-02 for AGENTS.md)
GPT says:    One combined Warning covering README.md, AGENTS.md, and architecture.md
Gemini says: One Critical finding covering README.md and AGENTS.md
Assessment: Gemini's Critical classification reflects that the Phase 1 relocation
checklist explicitly requires updating all consumers. However, the actual impact is
documentation staleness — no runtime failure, no data loss — which better fits
Warning in this project's severity taxonomy. Claude and GPT's Warning classification
is more appropriate. Resolution: treat as Warning in the synthesis (U-W-01), with the
note that AGENTS.md's reach (injected into every agent context) makes this closer to
the Critical boundary than a typical doc drift.
Resolution: Classified as Warning in U-W-01.
```

```
[D-02] Scope of stale .opencode/agents/ references
Claude says: Two files need updating — README.md and AGENTS.md
GPT says:    Four surfaces need updating — README.md, AGENTS.md, architecture.md,
             and savepoint_manager.py comment
Gemini says: Two files need updating — README.md and AGENTS.md
Assessment: GPT's broader scan is correct — both architecture.md and the savepoint
comment were independently verified as stale. Claude and Gemini scoped their findings
to the most visible consumer files. No contradiction, only difference in coverage
depth. GPT's additional surfaces are genuine and treated as singular findings S-I-01
and S-I-03.
Resolution: U-W-01 covers the two agreed surfaces; S-I-01 and S-I-03 cover GPT's
additional verified surfaces.
```

```
[D-03] Test coverage adequacy
Claude says: Suggestion — "agents" subdir missing from expected_subdirs list (S-02)
GPT says:    Warning — count-based assertion weakened and no longer proves the moved
             prompt set is intact (W-03)
Gemini says: No finding in this area
Assessment: Both observations are correct and describe the same root problem from
different angles: the regression test was loosened in a way that defeats its stated
purpose. Two models flagged this independently; escalating from Suggestion to Warning
is appropriate given the explicit docstring promise. Classified as M-W-01 at Warning.
Resolution: Majority finding M-W-01 at Warning severity.
```

## Overall Assessment

**Not ready to merge without fixes.** The core implementation (loader, handoffs, tests) is sound and all three models praised it. The blocking gap is the incomplete relocation follow-through: at minimum items 1 and 2 (the unanimous finding and the majority test finding) should be resolved before merge. Items 3–5 are confirmed stale references that, while not runtime-breaking, add maintenance debt and should be addressed in the same PR or an immediate follow-up.
